title: A sprint's goal can be rewritten by the operator when a gate re-answer narrows a clause
goal: Retrospective of SP-qxcj7fgy: the operator re-answered ST-yn3fa5ts gate g2 at the start so release keeps classing push, but set refuses goal on a sprint, so the sprint goal and close --summary still name a clause (a bare release no longer classes push) that the sprint deliberately does not deliver, recorded only in the sprint's notes. set SP --goal G --by operator rewrites a planned or active sprint's goal, or close --summary marks a clause narrowed by a gate answer recorded in the sprint's notes.

run: import json,os,subprocess,sys,tempfile; t=tempfile.mkdtemp(); os.makedirs(t+"/_backlog"); f=t+"/_backlog/SP-testtest.json"; open(f,"w").write(json.dumps({"id":"SP-testtest","kind":"sprint","title":"t","status":"active","goal":"old"})); p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/backlog.py","--root",t,"set","SP-testtest","--goal","new","--by","operator"],capture_output=True,text=True); sys.exit(0 if p.returncode==0 and json.load(open(f))["goal"]=="new" else 1)
